category: Phrasal verbs on regular bases: Q-S

entries.meaning: To form a line and wait your turn. ---
examples: Fans queued up overnight for tickets.
People were queuing up around the block by six.
You have to queue up at the counter to check in.
entries.русский: выстраиваться в очередь, выстроиться в очередь; стоять в очереди
entries.separable: no object — queue up at the door; nothing ever stands between queue and up
entries.forms: queue up · queued up · queued up

entries.meaning: To line something up so that it plays or runs next. ---
examples: Queue up the next song while I get drinks.
I queued up four episodes for the flight.
He's queuing the print jobs up to run overnight.
entries.русский: ставить, поставить в очередь (на воспроизведение, на выполнение); включать, включить следующим
entries.separable: separable — queue up the next episode, queue the next episode up, queue it up
entries.forms: queue up · queued up · queued up

entries.meaning: To become calmer and less noisy, or to make someone become that way. ---
examples: Quiet down — the movie's starting.
The crowd quieted down when the lights went out.
He spent ten minutes quieting the twins down.
entries.русский: успокаиваться, успокоиться; затихать, затихнуть; успокаивать, успокоить
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — quiet the baby down, quiet him down; with no object nothing splits it: everybody quieted down
entries.forms: quiet down · quieted down · quieted down
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (the class quieted down), transitive (she quieted the baby down)

entries.meaning: To build up a large total of something, especially points, wins, or debt. ---
examples: They rack up frequent-flyer miles on every trip.
The team racked up forty points in the first half.
He's been racking up credit card debt since college.
entries.русский: набирать, набрать; накапливать, накопить; наращивать, нарастить
entries.separable: separable — rack up points, rack up a huge bill; a pronoun goes in the middle: rack them up
entries.forms: rack up · racked up · racked up

entries.meaning: To force a game or an outdoor event to be canceled or stopped because of rain. ---
examples: Saturday's game was rained out.
A storm like that rains out every field in the county.
If we get rained out, your ticket is good for the next home game.
entries.русский: отменять, отменить из-за дождя; срывать, сорвать дождём
entries.separable: separable in theory — the storm rained out the tournament — but you will nearly always meet it in the passive: the game was rained out
entries.forms: rain out · rained out · rained out

entries.meaning: To earn or collect a large amount of money quickly and easily. ---
examples: The movie raked in forty million on its first weekend.
That food truck must be raking it in on game days.
They have raked in millions from a single app.
entries.русский: загребать, грести лопатой (деньги); сколачивать, сколотить (состояние)
entries.separable: separable — rake in the cash, rake the cash in, rake it in; the bare raking it in needs no real object at all
entries.forms: rake in · raked in · raked in

entries.meaning: To bring up something unpleasant from the past that people would rather forget. ---
examples: Why rake up a quarrel that everyone has forgotten?
The article raked up an old scandal from his college years.
Every election someone comes along raking that rumor up again.
entries.русский: ворошить (прошлое); вытаскивать на свет, припоминать (старое)
entries.separable: separable — rake up the past, rake the past up, rake it all up again; never ✗ rake up it
entries.forms: rake up · raked up · raked up

entries.meaning: To come together as a group to support someone who is in trouble. ---
examples: The neighborhood rallied around the family after the fire.
When she got sick, her coworkers rallied around.
They're rallying around their coach in a losing season.
entries.русский: сплачиваться, сплотиться вокруг; поддерживать, поддержать сообща
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows around: rally around him, never ✗ rally him around
entries.forms: rally around · rallied around · rallied around
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (the whole town rallied around), transitive (they rallied around her)

entries.meaning: To keep talking in a long, aimless way that bores the listener. ---
examples: He rambles on about his college days every Thanksgiving.
She rambled on for twenty minutes before getting to the point.
Sorry, I've been rambling on — your turn.
entries.русский: болтать без умолку; разглагольствовать; тянуть, растянуть речь
entries.separable: no object — nothing comes between ramble and on; the topic follows about: ramble on about the weather
entries.forms: ramble on · rambled on · rambled on

entries.meaning: To increase something steadily over a period, or to increase in that way. ---
examples: The plant ramps up production every fall.
They ramped up security after the threat.
Hiring has been ramping up since January.
entries.русский: наращивать, нарастить; увеличивать, увеличить; набирать, набрать обороты
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — ramp up production, ramp production up, ramp it up
entries.forms: ramp up · ramped up · ramped up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (ramp up production), intransitive (production is ramping up)

entries.meaning: To tell someone in authority what another person did, betraying them. ---
examples: Nobody wanted to rat out a teammate.
His own brother ratted him out.
She isn't ratting anyone out.
entries.русский: доносить, донести (на кого-л.); сдавать, сдать; выдавать, выдать
entries.separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — rat him out, never ✗ rat out him
entries.forms: rat out · ratted out · ratted out

entries.meaning: To say a list of things quickly and easily from memory. ---
examples: She can rattle off every state capital.
He rattled off the names of all twelve players.
The waiter was rattling the specials off too fast to follow.
entries.русский: выпаливать, выпалить; тараторить; перечислять, перечислить скороговоркой
entries.separable: separable — rattle off the names, rattle the names off, rattle them off
entries.forms: rattle off · rattled off · rattled off

entries.meaning: To get in touch with someone, usually to offer or ask for something. ---
examples: Reach out to me if anything changes.
A recruiter reached out last week.
We've been reaching out to every family on the list.
entries.русский: обращаться, обратиться (к кому-л.); связываться, связаться
entries.separable: inseparable — nothing splits it; the person follows to: reach out to her, never ✗ reach her out
entries.forms: reach out · reached out · reached out
entries.transitivity: intransitive — the person you contact follows to: reach out to the landlord

entries.meaning: To try to persuade someone by calm argument rather than force. ---
examples: There's no reasoning with him when he's angry.
I reasoned with her for an hour and got nowhere.
Somebody needs to reason with the landlord before this goes to court.
entries.русский: уговаривать, уговорить; вразумлять, вразумить; урезонивать, урезонить
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows with: reason with him, never ✗ reason him with
entries.forms: reason with · reasoned with · reasoned with
entries.transitivity: transitive — with with before the object

entries.meaning: To take someone or something seriously as a force you cannot ignore. ---
examples: Any new law has to reckon with the courts.
They hadn't reckoned with the cost of shipping.
She's a candidate to be reckoned with.
entries.русский: считаться с (кем-л., чем-л.); принимать, принять в расчёт; учитывать, учесть
entries.separable: inseparable — the object always follows with: reckon with the cost, never ✗ reckon the cost with
entries.forms: reckon with · reckoned with · reckoned with
entries.transitivity: transitive — with with before the object

entries.meaning: To attract someone and gradually draw them into doing what you want. ---
examples: The free trial reels people in.
They reeled in two big clients last quarter.
That ad has been reeling in thousands of sign-ups a day.
entries.русский: заманивать, заманить; привлекать, привлечь; заполучать, заполучить
entries.separable: separable — reel in new customers, reel customers in, reel them in
entries.forms: reel in · reeled in · reeled in

entries.meaning: To recite a long list quickly and without hesitating. ---
examples: He can reel off every president in order.
She reeled off six reasons without pausing.
The guide kept reeling dates off as we walked.
entries.русский: тараторить; выпаливать, выпалить; перечислять, перечислить без запинки
entries.separable: separable — reel off the dates, reel the dates off, reel them off
entries.forms: reel off · reeled off · reeled off

entries.meaning: To win or achieve a run of things one right after another. ---
examples: The Yankees reeled off nine straight wins in July.
She reels off three aces in a row whenever she's behind.
They've been reeling off record quarters since the merger.
entries.русский: выдавать, выдать серию (побед); одерживать, одержать подряд
entries.separable: separable — reel off five straight wins, reel them off
entries.forms: reel off · reeled off · reeled off

entries.meaning: To bring something or someone under control or hold them back. ---
examples: Congress wants to rein in spending.
The coach reined him in after the third foul.
They're reining in costs in every department.
entries.русский: обуздывать, обуздать; сдерживать, сдержать; ограничивать, ограничить
entries.separable: separable — rein in spending, rein spending in, rein it in
entries.forms: rein in · reined in · reined in

entries.meaning: To let someone use your property or equipment in exchange for regular payment. ---
examples: They rent out the basement to a student.
We rented out the cabin all summer.
She's renting her apartment out while she's abroad.
entries.русский: сдавать, сдать в аренду; сдавать, сдать внаём
entries.separable: separable — rent out the basement, rent the basement out, rent it out
entries.forms: rent out · rented out · rented out

entries.meaning: To come back and tell someone what you found out or what happened. ---
examples: Go look at the site and report back.
The task force reported back in March.
She's reporting back to the board on Friday.
entries.русский: докладывать, доложить (о результатах); отчитываться, отчитаться
entries.separable: no object — nothing splits it; the person you tell follows to and the subject follows on: report back to me on the numbers
entries.forms: report back · reported back · reported back

entries.meaning: To rest so that you have your strength back for something ahead. ---
examples: Rest up — tomorrow is a long day.
He rested up for a week before the marathon.
She's resting up after surgery.
entries.русский: отдыхать, отдохнуть как следует; набираться, набраться сил
entries.separable: no object — rest up before the trip; nothing goes between the two words
entries.forms: rest up · rested up · rested up

entries.meaning: To make an engine run faster and louder, or for an engine to do this. ---
examples: He revved up the motorcycle at every light.
Don't rev the engine up when it's cold.
A bus was revving up outside the window.
entries.русский: разгонять, разогнать (двигатель); газовать; заводить, завести мотор
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — rev up the engine, rev the engine up, rev it up
entries.forms: rev up · revved up · revved up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (rev up the engine), intransitive (the truck revved up outside)

entries.meaning: To make someone or something more excited or more active, or to become that way. ---
examples: The opening act revved up the crowd.
Hiring revs up every fall.
The campaign has been revving up since the debate.
entries.русский: раззадоривать, раззадорить; заводить, завести (публику); набирать, набрать обороты
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — rev up the crowd, rev the crowd up, rev them up
entries.forms: rev up · revved up · revved up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (rev up the crowd), intransitive (hiring is revving up)

entries.meaning: To put something together quickly out of whatever materials are at hand. ---
examples: Dad rigged up a shower with a garden hose and a bucket.
We can rig something up with duct tape until the part arrives.
They had rigged up lights over the whole driveway.
entries.русский: сооружать, соорудить (на скорую руку); мастерить, смастерить
entries.separable: separable — rig up a shelter, rig a shelter up, rig it up; never ✗ rig up it
entries.forms: rig up · rigged up · rigged up

entries.meaning: To wash something, or yourself, quickly with clean water. ---
examples: Rinse off the lettuce before you cut it.
He rinsed the soap off and got out of the shower.
I'm rinsing off — give me five minutes.
entries.русский: ополаскивать, ополоснуть; смывать, смыть; наскоро мыться, помыться
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — rinse off the sand, rinse the sand off, rinse it off; with no object it stands alone: let me rinse off
entries.forms: rinse off · rinsed off · rinsed off
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (rinse off the plates), intransitive (I need to rinse off)

entries.meaning: To clean the inside of something with water, or to wash a substance out of cloth or hair. ---
examples: Rinse out the bottle before you recycle it.
She rinsed the paint out with cold water.
I've rinsed out two shirts in the sink.
entries.русский: прополаскивать, прополоскать; споласкивать, сполоснуть
entries.separable: separable — rinse out the cup, rinse the cup out, rinse it out
entries.forms: rinse out · rinsed out · rinsed out

entries.meaning: To criticize or attack someone fiercely. ---
examples: The coach ripped into the team at halftime.
Reviewers have ripped into the new season.
She's ripping into him for missing the deadline.
entries.русский: набрасываться, наброситься (с критикой); разносить, разнести; отчитывать, отчитать
entries.separable: inseparable — the target follows into: rip into him, never ✗ rip him into
entries.forms: rip into · ripped into · ripped into
entries.transitivity: transitive — with into before the object

entries.meaning: To charge someone far too much or cheat them out of their money. ---
examples: That lot near the stadium rips off everybody.
We got ripped off on the rental car.
He knew he was being ripped off and paid anyway.
entries.русский: обдирать, ободрать; обсчитывать, обсчитать; надувать, надуть
entries.separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — they ripped me off, never ✗ ripped off me; a full noun goes either way: rip off tourists, rip tourists off
entries.forms: rip off · ripped off · ripped off

entries.meaning: To copy someone else's work or idea without permission or credit. ---
examples: The chorus rips off an old Motown song.
They ripped off our logo almost line for line.
He's been accused of ripping off a rival designer.
entries.русский: красть, украсть (идею); передирать, передрать; заимствовать без спроса
entries.separable: separable — rip off a melody, rip the melody off, rip it off
entries.forms: rip off · ripped off · ripped off

entries.meaning: To steal something. ---
examples: Somebody ripped off my bike outside the library.
They rip off three or four stores a month.
His laptop got ripped off at the airport.
entries.русский: красть, украсть; тырить, стырить; угонять, угнать
entries.separable: separable — rip off a car stereo, rip the stereo off, rip it off
entries.forms: rip off · ripped off · ripped off

entries.meaning: To pull something out roughly and completely. ---
examples: They ripped out the old carpet in an afternoon.
He ripped a page out of the notebook.
We're ripping out the kitchen next month.
entries.русский: вырывать, вырвать; сдирать, содрать; выдирать, выдрать
entries.separable: separable — rip out the wiring, rip the wiring out, rip it out
entries.forms: rip out · ripped out · ripped out

entries.meaning: To move through a place very fast and cause damage. ---
examples: A tornado ripped through the county overnight.
Fire rips through dry brush in minutes.
The flu has been ripping through the office all week.
entries.русский: проноситься, пронестись (сметая всё); прокатываться, прокатиться; охватывать, охватить
entries.separable: inseparable — the place follows through: rip through the town, never ✗ rip the town through
entries.forms: rip through · ripped through · ripped through
entries.transitivity: transitive — with through before the object

entries.meaning: To tear something into pieces, or to cancel an agreement as if tearing it up. ---
examples: He ripped up the parking ticket.
They're threatening to rip the contract up.
She has ripped up every photo of him.
entries.русский: рвать, разорвать на куски; разрывать, разорвать; аннулировать
entries.separable: separable — rip up the check, rip the check up, rip it up
entries.forms: rip up · ripped up · ripped up

entries.meaning: To reduce something to an earlier level, or to undo a change that was made. ---
examples: The store rolled back prices for the weekend.
The new rule rolls back protections passed in 2019.
They're rolling the update back after the bug reports.
entries.русский: снижать, снизить (до прежнего уровня); отменять, отменить; откатывать, откатить назад
entries.separable: separable — roll back prices, roll prices back, roll them back
entries.forms: roll back · rolled back · rolled back

entries.meaning: To arrive somewhere late and without hurrying. ---
examples: He rolled in twenty minutes after the meeting started.
They roll in around noon on Sundays.
She came rolling in at midnight with no explanation.
entries.русский: являться, явиться (не спеша, с опозданием); заваливаться, завалиться
entries.separable: no object — nothing splits it: he rolled in late
entries.forms: roll in · rolled in · rolled in

entries.meaning: To keep arriving in large amounts. ---
examples: Once the reviews are good, the bookings just roll in.
Donations rolled in after the story aired.
Orders have been rolling in faster than we can fill them.
entries.русский: поступать, поступить в большом количестве; сыпаться, посыпаться; валить, повалить
entries.separable: no object — the thing arriving is the subject: the orders rolled in
entries.forms: roll in · rolled in · rolled in

entries.meaning: To introduce a new product, service, or program, often in stages. ---
examples: They roll out the new app in June.
The company rolled out the policy store by store.
We're rolling the update out to everyone this week.
entries.русский: выпускать, выпустить; запускать, запустить; вводить, ввести (поэтапно)
entries.separable: separable — roll out a new plan, roll the plan out, roll it out
entries.forms: roll out · rolled out · rolled out

entries.meaning: To move money or an unused amount into the next period or account instead of losing it. ---
examples: Unused data rolls over to the next month.
She rolled over her 401(k) when she changed jobs.
The jackpot has rolled over three weeks running.
entries.русский: переносить, перенести (на следующий период); переводить, перевести (средства на другой счёт)
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — roll over the balance, roll the balance over, roll it over
entries.forms: roll over · rolled over · rolled over
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (roll over your 401(k)), intransitive (unused minutes roll over)

entries.meaning: To stop resisting and give in without a fight. ---
examples: The defense just rolled over in the second half.
He rolled over the moment the lawyers called.
We're not rolling over on this one.
entries.русский: сдаваться, сдаться без борьбы; уступать, уступить; складывать, сложить лапки
entries.separable: no object — the team rolled over; what you give in on follows on: roll over on the price
entries.forms: roll over · rolled over · rolled over

entries.meaning: To arrive somewhere in a vehicle, often late or in no hurry. ---
examples: They rolled up two hours late in a borrowed van.
Guests kept rolling up long after the food was gone.
He will roll up around noon, the way he always does.
entries.русский: подъезжать, подъехать; заявляться, заявиться (с опозданием)
entries.separable: inseparable and intransitive here — roll up in a taxi, roll up at eleven; never ✗ roll something up
entries.forms: roll up · rolled up · rolled up

entries.meaning: To turn something flat into a tube, or to wind something upward. ---
examples: Roll up your sleeves — this is going to get messy.
He rolled the poster up and slid it into a tube.
She had rolled up the car window before the rain started.
entries.русский: сворачивать, свернуть (в трубку); закатывать, закатать (рукава); поднимать (стекло)
entries.separable: separable — roll up the map, roll the map up, roll it up; never ✗ roll up it
entries.forms: roll up · rolled up · rolled up

entries.meaning: To find something bad or hidden and get rid of it completely. ---
examples: The new director wants to root out waste.
They rooted out the bug after three days.
He's rooting out every dead link on the site.
entries.русский: искоренять, искоренить; выявлять, выявить и устранить; выкорчёвывать, выкорчевать
entries.separable: separable — root out corruption, root corruption out, root it out
entries.forms: root out · rooted out · rooted out

entries.meaning: To talk someone into helping with something they had not planned to do. ---
examples: They're always roping in a few parents to drive.
He roped me in to help him move.
I keep getting roped into planning the party.
entries.русский: втягивать, втянуть; вовлекать, вовлечь; припрягать, припрячь
entries.separable: separable — rope in a few volunteers, rope him in; the job follows into: rope him into painting the fence
entries.forms: rope in · roped in · roped in

entries.meaning: To close off an area with rope or tape so that people cannot enter it. ---
examples: Police roped off the whole block.
They rope off the front rows for the family.
The museum had roped the painting off.
entries.русский: огораживать, огородить; оцеплять, оцепить; перекрывать, перекрыть
entries.separable: separable — rope off the area, rope the area off, rope it off
entries.forms: rope off · roped off · roped off

entries.meaning: To handle someone violently and hurt them, short of a real beating. ---
examples: Two guys roughed him up behind the bar.
The suspect says the officers roughed him up.
They're not above roughing up a witness.
entries.русский: избивать, избить; поколотить; помять (кого-л.)
entries.separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — rough him up, never ✗ rough up him
entries.forms: rough up · roughed up · roughed up

entries.meaning: To lower a number to the nearest whole or convenient figure below it. ---
examples: Round down to the nearest hundred.
The register rounded the price down to nine dollars.
We're rounding down to keep the estimate safe.
entries.русский: округлять, округлить в меньшую сторону
entries.separable: separable — round down the total, round the total down, round it down
entries.forms: round down · rounded down · rounded down
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (round the price down), intransitive (anything under .5 rounds down)

entries.meaning: To change a number to the nearest simpler one. ---
examples: Round off the total to the nearest dollar.
He rounded off 3.7 to 4.
The report rounds every figure off to two decimals.
entries.русский: округлять, округлить (число)
entries.separable: separable — round off the figures, round the figures off, round them off
entries.forms: round off · rounded off · rounded off

entries.meaning: To end something in a satisfying way. ---
examples: We rounded off the meal with coffee and pie.
A win on Sunday would round off a great season.
They're rounding off the tour in Chicago.
entries.русский: завершать, завершить; заканчивать, закончить (чем-л. приятным)
entries.separable: separable — round off the evening, round the evening off, round it off
entries.forms: round off · rounded off · rounded off

entries.meaning: To add what is missing so that something is complete and balanced. ---
examples: Two more hires would round out the team.
Dessert rounded out the meal nicely.
They're rounding out the roster with a backup goalie.
entries.русский: дополнять, дополнить; доукомплектовывать, доукомплектовать; завершать, завершить состав
entries.separable: separable — round out the lineup, round the lineup out, round it out
entries.forms: round out · rounded out · rounded out

entries.meaning: To gather people, animals, or things together into one place. ---
examples: Can you round up a few volunteers?
Police rounded up six suspects overnight.
He's rounding the kids up for dinner.
entries.русский: собирать, собрать (вместе); сгонять, согнать; задерживать, задержать (о полиции)
entries.separable: separable — round up the horses, round the horses up, round them up
entries.forms: round up · rounded up · rounded up

entries.meaning: To raise a number to the next whole or convenient figure. ---
examples: The app rounds up every purchase and saves the change.
I rounded it up to twenty dollars.
If you're rounding up, call it two hours.
entries.русский: округлять, округлить в большую сторону
entries.separable: separable — round up the total, round the total up, round it up
entries.forms: round up · rounded up · rounded up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (round the bill up), intransitive (.5 and above rounds up)

entries.meaning: To dry or massage a person or animal by rubbing them hard all over. ---
examples: The trainer rubbed the pitcher's shoulder down with ice.
Always rub down a horse after a long ride.
She was rubbing the dog down with an old beach towel.
entries.русский: растирать, растереть; обтирать, обтереть (насухо); массировать
entries.separable: separable — rub down the horse, rub the horse down, rub him down; never ✗ rub down him
entries.forms: rub down · rubbed down · rubbed down

entries.meaning: To keep mentioning something that embarrasses or upsets another person. ---
examples: I know I lost — don't rub it in.
He rubbed it in for a week.
She kept rubbing in how much cheaper her ticket had been.
entries.русский: злорадно напоминать; сыпать соль на рану; тыкать носом
entries.separable: separable, and the object is almost always it: rub it in. ✗ rub in it is impossible
entries.forms: rub in · rubbed in · rubbed in

entries.meaning: To come away from a surface because something has rubbed against it. ---
examples: The price sticker rubbed off in my pocket.
Fresh ink will rub off if you close the book too soon.
Half the paint had rubbed off the railing over the winter.
entries.русский: стираться, стереться; сходить, сойти (о краске, надписи)
entries.separable: intransitive here, so nothing comes between; where the mark lands takes on: rubbed off on my sleeve
entries.forms: rub off · rubbed off · rubbed off

entries.meaning: To remove a mark or a coating by rubbing it. ---
examples: Rub the chalk off the board before the next class.
He rubbed off the pencil line and started the drawing again.
The engraving has been rubbed off by a century of hands.
entries.русский: стирать, стереть (трением); оттирать, оттереть
entries.separable: separable — rub off the chalk, rub the chalk off, rub it off; never ✗ rub off it
entries.forms: rub off · rubbed off · rubbed off

entries.meaning: To pass from one person to another, of a habit, mood, or quality. ---
examples: Her optimism rubs off on everyone in the room.
Some of his bad habits have rubbed off on me.
You can see the coach's style rubbing off on the younger players.
entries.русский: передаваться, передаться (кому-л.); влиять, повлиять (о привычках, настроении)
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows on: rub off on him, never ✗ rub him off on
entries.forms: rub off on · rubbed off on · rubbed off on
entries.third person: rubs off on · -ing form: rubbing off on
entries.transitivity: transitive — with on before the person it reaches

entries.meaning: To murder someone, in gangster slang. ---
examples: The boss had him rubbed out before he could testify.
They rubbed out two rivals in the same week.
Nobody would dare rub him out in his own club.
entries.русский: убивать, убить; приканчивать, прикончить (сленг)
entries.separable: separable — rub out a witness, rub him out; old crime-movie slang, and always about a person
entries.forms: rub out · rubbed out · rubbed out

entries.meaning: To remove writing or pencil marks by rubbing them away. ---
examples: Rub that line out and try the sum again.
She rubbed out the wrong date and wrote the right one above it.
Someone had rubbed out half the names on the list.
entries.русский: стирать, стереть (ластиком); вычёркивать, вычеркнуть
entries.separable: separable — rub out the answer, rub the answer out, rub it out; never ✗ rub out it. For pencil marks Americans more often say erase
entries.forms: rub out · rubbed out · rubbed out

entries.meaning: To decide that something is impossible or will not happen. ---
examples: Doctors have ruled out anything serious.
She hasn't ruled out running again.
The weather rules a picnic out.
entries.русский: исключать, исключить; отвергать, отвергнуть (как невозможное)
entries.separable: separable — rule out a strike, rule a strike out, rule it out
entries.forms: rule out · ruled out · ruled out

entries.meaning: To do something important too quickly, without enough thought. ---
examples: Don't rush into a decision you'll regret.
They rushed into marriage after two months.
He's rushing into it because the price expires tonight.
entries.русский: бросаться, броситься очертя голову; торопиться, поторопиться с (решением)
entries.separable: inseparable — what you hurry into follows into: rush into a contract. With a person it becomes rush someone into something: don't rush me into signing
entries.forms: rush into · rushed into · rushed into
entries.transitivity: transitive — with into before the object

entries.meaning: To deal with something too quickly, or to push it through a process at speed. ---
examples: Congress rushed the bill through before the recess.
Don't rush through the instructions.
They're rushing her through admissions now.
entries.русский: спешно проводить, провести; протаскивать, протащить (закон); делать, сделать наспех
entries.separable: separable when something is pushed through a process — rush the order through, rush it through; with the object after the particle it means doing something fast: rush through dinner
entries.forms: rush through · rushed through · rushed through

entries.meaning: To make or find something quickly out of whatever is available, especially food. ---
examples: I'll rustle up some sandwiches.
He rustled up three volunteers in an hour.
She's rustling up dinner from what's left in the fridge.
entries.русский: наспех готовить, приготовить; раздобывать, раздобыть; сообразить (на скорую руку)
entries.separable: separable — rustle up a meal, rustle a meal up, rustle it up
entries.forms: rustle up · rustled up · rustled up

entries.meaning: To get through a test, a task, or a hard stretch of time easily and with no trouble. ---
examples: She sails through every exam without studying.
The bill sailed through the Senate in a day.
He's sailing through his first semester.
entries.русский: легко справляться, легко справиться; проходить, пройти без труда
entries.separable: inseparable — through keeps hold of its object: sailed through the test, sailed through it; never ✗ sailed the test through
entries.forms: sail through · sailed through · sailed through

entries.meaning: To save money quietly over a long time, or hide it where no one will look. ---
examples: He had salted away enough to buy the place outright.
She salts a little away from every paycheck.
They spent years quietly salting away cash in offshore accounts.
entries.русский: откладывать, отложить (деньги); припрятывать, припрятать
entries.separable: separable — salt away money, salt the money away, salt it away; never ✗ salt away it
entries.forms: salt away · salted away · salted away

entries.meaning: To put money aside little by little over time in order to buy something. ---
examples: They're saving up for a trip to Italy.
I saved up all summer to buy that bike.
He's saved up almost three thousand dollars.
entries.русский: копить, накопить; откладывать, отложить (деньги)
entries.separable: separable, but it usually stands alone or takes for: saving up for a car; with an amount both orders work — saved up $3,000, saved it up over a year
entries.forms: save up · saved up · saved up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (we're saving up), transitive (saved up enough for the deposit)

entries.meaning: To reduce how big, expensive, or ambitious a plan is. ---
examples: The city scaled back its renovation plans.
We've scaled back the guest list to forty.
They're scaling the program back after the budget cut.
entries.русский: сокращать, сократить; урезать; свёртывать, свернуть (планы, расходы)
entries.separable: separable — scale back the project, scale the project back, scale it back; never ✗ scale back it
entries.forms: scale back · scaled back · scaled back
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (scaled back production), intransitive (the airline scaled back after the crisis)

entries.meaning: To make something smaller while keeping the same shape or proportions. ---
examples: The design was scaled down to fit the lot.
They're scaling down the whole operation.
We scaled the drawing down by half.
entries.русский: уменьшать, уменьшить; сокращать, сократить (размер, масштаб)
entries.separable: separable — scale down the model, scale the model down, scale it down
entries.forms: scale down · scaled down · scaled down

entries.meaning: To make something much bigger, especially to turn a small operation into a large one. ---
examples: The company is trying to scale up without hiring.
They scaled up production after the first big order.
We've scaled the pilot up to twelve schools.
entries.русский: увеличивать, увеличить; наращивать, нарастить (объёмы); расширять, расширить
entries.separable: separable — scale up production, scale production up, scale it up
entries.forms: scale up · scaled up · scaled up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (scaled up production), intransitive (the startup is scaling up fast)

entries.meaning: To frighten a person or animal into going away, or to make a buyer lose interest. ---
examples: The dog scares off anyone who comes near the gate.
High prices scared off most buyers.
You're scaring him off with all these questions.
entries.русский: отпугивать, отпугнуть; спугивать, спугнуть
entries.separable: separable — scare off the deer, scare the deer off, and a pronoun must go in the middle: scare them off, never ✗ scare off them
entries.forms: scare off · scared off · scared off

entries.meaning: To manage to find or put together something out of whatever happens to be available. ---
examples: See if you can scare up a few more chairs.
He scared up enough cash for a bus ticket.
We're scaring up volunteers for Saturday.
entries.русский: раздобывать, раздобыть; наскребать, наскрести
entries.separable: separable — scare up some chairs, scare some chairs up, scare them up
entries.forms: scare up · scared up · scared up

entries.meaning: To eat something very fast. ---
examples: He scarfed down two slices and ran for the bus.
They scarf down whatever's in the fridge.
She's scarfing her lunch down at her desk.
entries.русский: уплетать, уплести; жадно съедать, съесть; уминать, умять
entries.separable: separable — scarf down a sandwich, scarf a sandwich down, scarf it down
entries.forms: scarf down · scarfed down · scarfed down

entries.meaning: To buy or take something quickly, before anyone else can get it. ---
examples: Fans scooped up the tickets in an hour.
Investors are scooping up cheap houses.
She scooped the last two up before I got there.
entries.русский: расхватывать, расхватать; быстро скупать, скупить
entries.separable: separable — scoop up the tickets, scoop the tickets up, scoop them up
entries.forms: scoop up · scooped up · scooped up

entries.meaning: To move a short way sideways so that someone else has room to sit. ---
examples: Can you scoot over a little?
He scooted over so she could sit down.
Everyone was scooting over to make room for the twins.
entries.русский: подвигаться, подвинуться; сдвигаться, сдвинуться (освобождая место)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; nothing ever comes between scoot and over
entries.forms: scoot over · scooted over · scooted over

entries.meaning: To look a place or a situation over carefully in advance, to see what it is like. ---
examples: Let's scope out the parking situation first.
We scoped the venue out last weekend.
He's been scoping out colleges all fall.
entries.русский: разведывать, разведать; присматриваться, присмотреться; осматривать, осмотреть заранее
entries.separable: separable — scope out the place, scope the place out, scope it out
entries.forms: scope out · scoped out · scoped out

entries.meaning: To search an area in order to find something suitable. ---
examples: They scouted out three possible campsites.
I'll scout a route out before we drive it.
She's scouting out office space downtown.
entries.русский: подыскивать, подыскать; разведывать, разведать
entries.separable: separable — scout out a campsite, scout a campsite out, scout it out
entries.forms: scout out · scouted out · scouted out

entries.meaning: To manage to live or succeed with barely enough money or barely enough ability. ---
examples: They scrape by on one paycheck.
We scraped by that first winter.
He's been scraping by since the layoff.
entries.русский: перебиваться, перебиться; еле сводить концы с концами
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you live on follows on: scrape by on one paycheck
entries.forms: scrape by · scraped by · scraped by

entries.meaning: To succeed at something by the smallest possible margin. ---
examples: He scraped through the final with a sixty-one.
If I study tonight, I might scrape through.
The bill has scraped through the Senate by two votes.
entries.русский: еле сдавать, сдать; с трудом проходить, пройти; еле-еле справляться
entries.separable: inseparable — scrape through the exam, or with no object at all: he just scraped through; never ✗ scrape the exam through
entries.forms: scrape through · scraped through · scraped through
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (scraped through the test), intransitive (he just scraped through)

entries.meaning: To manage with difficulty to collect enough money, people, or material. ---
examples: We scraped together enough for the deposit.
She's scraping together a team for Saturday.
They scraped the money together somehow.
entries.русский: наскребать, наскрести; с трудом собирать, собрать
entries.separable: separable — scrape together the rent, scrape the rent together, scrape it together
entries.forms: scrape together · scraped together · scraped together

entries.meaning: To remove unwanted people or things by checking them against a standard. ---
examples: The filter screens out most junk mail.
Two rounds of tests screened out half the applicants.
They're screening the weaker bids out first.
entries.русский: отсеивать, отсеять; отфильтровывать, отфильтровать
entries.separable: separable — screen out spam, screen spam out, screen it out
entries.forms: screen out · screened out · screened out

entries.meaning: To waste time instead of doing what you are supposed to be doing. ---
examples: Quit screwing around and finish your homework.
We screwed around all afternoon.
He's been screwing around with the code instead of fixing the bug.
entries.русский: валять дурака; бездельничать; тратить, потратить время впустую
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you are fiddling with follows with: screwing around with the settings
entries.forms: screw around · screwed around · screwed around

entries.meaning: To treat someone very unfairly, usually for your own gain. ---
examples: The landlord screwed them over on the deposit.
He screwed over everyone who trusted him.
I'm not going to screw you over.
entries.русский: кидать, кинуть; обманывать, обмануть; поступать, поступить подло с
entries.separable: separable, and a pronoun must split it: screwed me over, never ✗ screwed over me; with a noun both orders work — screwed over his partner, screwed his partner over
entries.forms: screw over · screwed over · screwed over

entries.meaning: To make a bad mistake, or to ruin something by handling it badly. ---
examples: I screwed up the dates on the invitation.
Don't screw this up.
He's been screwing up at work all month.
entries.русский: портачить, напортачить; портить, испортить; лажать, облажаться
entries.separable: separable — screw up the order, screw the order up, screw it up; very often with no object at all: I screwed up
entries.forms: screw up · screwed up · screwed up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (sorry, I screwed up), transitive (screwed up the whole schedule)

entries.meaning: To close an area completely so that nobody can go in or out. ---
examples: Police sealed off the block within minutes.
They're sealing off the damaged wing.
The tunnel has been sealed off since the flood.
entries.русский: перекрывать, перекрыть; оцеплять, оцепить; изолировать (участок)
entries.separable: separable — seal off the street, seal the street off, seal it off
entries.forms: seal off · sealed off · sealed off

entries.meaning: Of a machine or a part of the body, to stop moving suddenly and stick. ---
examples: The engine seized up on the highway.
My back seizes up every time I lift something heavy.
Credit markets were seizing up by October.
entries.русский: заклинивать, заклинить; заедать, заесть; сводить, свести (о мышце)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the engine or the muscle is the subject, and nothing comes between the two words
entries.forms: seize up · seized up · seized up

entries.meaning: To put food in front of people, or to offer an audience something ready-made. ---
examples: They serve up the best pancakes in town.
He served up a three-course meal in an hour.
The show is serving up the same jokes it did last year.
entries.русский: подавать, подать (на стол); преподносить, преподнести
entries.separable: separable — serve up dinner, serve dinner up, serve it up
entries.forms: serve up · served up · served up

entries.meaning: To become calm and quiet, or to make someone calm and quiet. ---
examples: Settle down, everyone — the movie's starting.
It took an hour to settle the twins down.
The wind had settled down by evening.
entries.русский: успокаиваться, успокоиться; утихомириваться, утихомириться
entries.separable: separable when you calm someone else — settle the kids down, settle them down; most often it takes no object at all: settle down!
entries.forms: settle down · settled down · settled down
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (settle down, please), transitive (settled the class down)

entries.meaning: To begin a quiet, permanent life in one place, usually with a partner and a steady job. ---
examples: They settled down in a small town outside Austin.
He's not ready to settle down.
Her parents keep asking when she's settling down.
entries.русский: остепеняться, остепениться; обзаводиться, обзавестись домом и семьёй
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the place follows in: settled down in Austin
entries.forms: settle down · settled down · settled down

entries.meaning: To accept something less than what you wanted, because nothing better is on offer. ---
examples: We wanted a house, but we settled for a condo.
Don't settle for the first offer you get.
She's not settling for anything less than the lead role.
entries.русский: довольствоваться, удовольствоваться; соглашаться, согласиться на (меньшее)
entries.separable: inseparable — for holds its object: settled for second place, settled for it; never ✗ settled second place for
entries.forms: settle for · settled for · settled for

entries.meaning: To get used to a new home, job, or school and start feeling comfortable there. ---
examples: Give her a week to settle in.
We settled in faster than we expected.
He's still settling in at the new school.
entries.русский: обживаться, обжиться; осваиваться, освоиться (на новом месте)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the place takes at or in: settling in at the new office
entries.forms: settle in · settled in · settled in

entries.meaning: To make a final choice among several possibilities. ---
examples: They settled on the blue one in the end.
We've settled on a date for the wedding.
He's settling on a major this semester.
entries.русский: останавливаться, остановиться на; выбирать, выбрать окончательно
entries.separable: inseparable — settled on a name, settled on it; never ✗ settled a name on
entries.forms: settle on · settled on · settled on

entries.meaning: To pay what you owe so that nobody owes anybody anything. ---
examples: Let's settle up before you leave.
We settled up at the end of the trip.
He's settling up with the contractor now.
entries.русский: рассчитываться, рассчитаться; расплачиваться, расплатиться
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the person you owe follows with: settle up with the waiter
entries.forms: settle up · settled up · settled up

entries.meaning: To move in and live with a romantic partner without being married. ---
examples: They shacked up a month after they met.
Her parents were not thrilled that she wanted to shack up with him.
The two of them have been shacked up in a cabin all winter.
entries.русский: сожительствовать, жить вместе (без брака); съезжаться, съехаться
entries.separable: inseparable and intransitive — the partner takes with: shacked up with her boyfriend; informal, and often faintly disapproving
entries.forms: shack up · shacked up · shacked up

entries.meaning: To develop in a particular way, usually a promising one. ---
examples: The season is shaping up to be a good one.
Plans shaped up quickly after the meeting.
How is the new hire shaping up?
entries.русский: складываться, сложиться; вырисовываться, вырисоваться
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; usually followed by an adverb or by to be: shaping up nicely, shaping up to be a long night
entries.forms: shape up · shaped up · shaped up

entries.meaning: To start behaving or performing better. ---
examples: You'd better shape up or you'll be off the team.
He shaped up fast once the coach benched him.
The whole department is finally shaping up.
entries.русский: исправляться, исправиться; браться, взяться за ум; подтягиваться, подтянуться
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the two words never come apart
entries.forms: shape up · shaped up · shaped up

entries.meaning: To cut a small amount off a time, a price, or a piece of material — or hair off a face. ---
examples: The new route shaves off twenty minutes.
He shaved off his beard on a dare.
They're shaving a few dollars off the price.
entries.русский: сбривать, сбрить; скидывать, скинуть (время, цену)
entries.separable: separable — shave off twenty minutes, shave twenty minutes off, shave it off
entries.forms: shave off · shaved off · shaved off

entries.meaning: To pay a lot of money for something, usually unwillingly. ---
examples: We shelled out almost a thousand dollars for the repair.
Fans are shelling out $300 a ticket.
He's shelled out more than he can afford.
entries.русский: раскошеливаться, раскошелиться; выкладывать, выложить (деньги)
entries.separable: separable with an amount — shell out $200, shell it out; with no amount it takes for: shelled out for new tires
entries.forms: shell out · shelled out · shelled out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (shelled out four hundred bucks), intransitive (we shelled out for the good seats)

entries.meaning: To send someone away to a distant place, often whether they want to go or not. ---
examples: They shipped him off to boarding school.
Her parents ship her off to her grandmother's every July.
New recruits are being shipped off next week.
entries.русский: отправлять, отправить (кого-л. куда-л.); спроваживать, спровадить
entries.separable: separable — ship the kids off to camp, ship off the kids, ship them off
entries.forms: ship off · shipped off · shipped off

entries.meaning: To leave for a distant posting, especially in the military, or to send goods away to customers. ---
examples: His battalion ships out on Sunday.
We shipped out the last of the orders yesterday.
They're shipping out two hundred boxes a day.
entries.русский: отбывать, отбыть; отправляться, отправиться; отгружать, отгрузить
entries.separable: separable when goods are the object — ship out the orders, ship them out; with no object it means "leave": we ship out Monday
entries.forms: ship out · shipped out · shipped out
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (his unit ships out at dawn), transitive (they shipped out 400 units)

entries.meaning: To compare prices or offers at several places before you buy. ---
examples: Shop around before you sign anything.
We shopped around and saved two hundred dollars.
She's shopping around for a better rate.
entries.русский: приценяться, прицениться; искать, поискать, где дешевле
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you are looking for follows for: shop around for insurance
entries.forms: shop around · shopped around · shopped around

entries.meaning: To support something that is weak or failing so that it does not collapse. ---
examples: The loan shored up the company for another year.
They're shoring up the bridge before winter.
The mayor has shored up support among older voters.
entries.русский: подкреплять, подкрепить; укреплять, укрепить; поддерживать, поддержать
entries.separable: separable — shore up the economy, shore the economy up, shore it up
entries.forms: shore up · shored up · shored up

entries.meaning: To stop someone from being heard by shouting louder than they can speak. ---
examples: Protesters shouted down the mayor.
He was shouted down before he finished his first sentence.
They're shouting him down again.
entries.русский: перекрикивать, перекричать; заглушать, заглушить криками
entries.separable: separable — shout down the speaker, shout the speaker down, shout her down
entries.forms: shout down · shouted down · shouted down

entries.meaning: To say something loudly so that everyone can hear it. ---
examples: Kids were shouting out answers before she finished the question.
Someone shouted out my name in the crowd.
Shout out if you can't hear me in the back.
entries.русский: выкрикивать, выкрикнуть; громко называть, назвать
entries.separable: separable — shout out the answer, shout the answer out, shout it out; also used with no object: just shout out if you need help
entries.forms: shout out · shouted out · shouted out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (shouted out the numbers), intransitive (shout out if you can't hear)

entries.meaning: To leave or go away, often said as a rude order to someone you want rid of. ---
examples: He told the photographers to shove off.
The kid shoved off the moment he saw the manager coming.
We were shoving off just as the rain started.
entries.русский: убираться, убраться; проваливать; отчаливать, отчалить
entries.separable: inseparable and intransitive, and often a blunt order: shove off!
entries.forms: shove off · shoved off · shoved off

entries.meaning: To treat something unpleasant as unimportant and pay no attention to it. ---
examples: He shrugged off the insult and kept walking.
She shrugs off every bad review.
The team is shrugging the loss off.
entries.русский: отмахиваться, отмахнуться от; не придавать, не придать значения
entries.separable: separable — shrug off the criticism, shrug the criticism off, shrug it off
entries.forms: shrug off · shrugged off · shrugged off

entries.meaning: To avoid something because it makes you uneasy or afraid. ---
examples: He shies away from anything that looks like paperwork.
She never shied away from a hard question.
Investors are shying away from the whole sector.
entries.русский: избегать, избежать; уклоняться, уклониться от; сторониться
entries.separable: inseparable — the thing avoided always sits after from: shy away from conflict, shy away from it; never ✗ shy conflict away from
entries.forms: shy away from · shied away from · shied away from
entries.third person: shies away from · -ing form: shying away from

entries.meaning: To support one person or group in an argument or dispute. ---
examples: The court sided with the tenants.
My mom always sided with my sister.
Two senators are siding with the governor on this.
entries.русский: принимать, принять сторону; становиться, стать на сторону
entries.separable: inseparable — with keeps its object: sided with her brother, sided with him; never ✗ sided her brother with
entries.forms: side with · sided with · sided with

entries.meaning: To go through a large amount of material piece by piece in order to find something. ---
examples: Investigators sifted through hours of video.
I'm sifting through a box of old photos.
She has sifted through every résumé twice.
entries.русский: перебирать, перебрать; просматривать, просмотреть (в поисках чего-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — through keeps its object: sifting through the files, sifting through them; never ✗ sift the files through
entries.forms: sift through · sifted through · sifted through

entries.meaning: To give up a right or a claim by signing something, usually for good. ---
examples: Don't sign away your right to sue.
